newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady/off, feeders steady/up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady/off, feeders steady/up.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb lower while feeder cattle were called steady to up 0.100 cent, livestock analysts said.

Packers were seen bidding only $62 per cwt for cash cattle to start the week, down $1 from last week, and this should weigh on sentiment. Beef prices may also be under further pressure as the bulk of demand after the holiday will only come from fill-in business, analysts said.
Trade may be light in futures until the cash market establishes itself, they said.

Feeder cattle futures were seen showing carryover support following another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index and lower corn futures indications. Lower feed costs and a seasonal trend for feeder supplies to tighten should encourage support in feeders, analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.20 to $80.87 per cwt, the highest level since April 18, 1994.
